title: Evergreen Logistics POC scoping - commercial guardrails

transcript:
Meeting Header: Date: 2025-06-25 15:00 UTC; Duration: 52 minutes; Location: Zoom; Recording: yes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Mark Rivera (Evergreen CTO), Priya Sharma (Evergreen ML Engineer), Liam O'Neill (Head of Product), Rosa Kim (Procurement)

[00:00] Samira Patel (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intro from me and Jordan then would love to hear a bit about Evergreen's goals for the POC.
[00:18] Mark Rivera (CTO): Hey Samira, thanks. So, high level we want to move a couple of NLP features off our prototype infra into something production-grade, mainly doc summarization for drivers and a route optimization assistant that uses narrative prompts to help dispatch.
[00:36] Jordan Lee (SE): Cool, and are you currently running anything on open models or a managed API?
[00:44] Priya Sharma (ML Eng): We're mostly on a mix — some in-house fine-tuned models on SageMaker right now and some traffic to gpt-4 via API for heavier tasks, costs are getting a bit out of hand.
[01:02] Samira Patel (AE): Got it. Two typical levers we talk about: hosting mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and optimizations like quantization/batching to hit cost and latency. For the POC we're proposing a 6-week pilot, does that match your expectation?
[01:18] Mark Rivera: Yeah 6 weeks sounds reasonable as long as we can show clear metrics. Key internally is latency — P95 — and cost per thousand tokens. If we don't hit near-parity with our current baseline we probably won't move forward.
[01:34] Liam O'Neill (Product): Also quality: summaries must be within 2 points of our human evals on our internal rubric. If quality drops, it's a no-go even if cheaper.
[01:48] Jordan Lee: Understood. Can you give ballpark traffic? avg tokens per request, concurrency?
[01:55] Priya Sharma: Average prompt+response around 512 tokens, bursts to ~1k for long documents. Concurrency we expect 6-10 concurrent requests for the critical path, peak qps maybe 20 for short-lived spikes.
[02:12] Jordan Lee: Great that's super helpful. For benchmarking we'll simulate your traffic shape, run load tests to measure tail latency and throughput, and run quality evals on your sample prompts.
[02:26] Rosa Kim (Procurement): Quick question on the commercial side — what does a POC usually look like from costs and credits? We have procurement blackout in mid-July so timelines matter.
[02:38] Samira Patel: Thanks Rosa. For a standard 6-week POC Redwood typically offers a mix of pilot credits and time-limited terms. For this profile we'd propose $15k in pilot credits or equivalent token quota, plus a 6-week pilot agreement. If you need more runway we can extend or convert to a paid trial.
[02:56] Rosa Kim: Is that $15k a fixed number, or can it be token-based? We try to budget by tokens.
[03:03] Samira Patel: We can structure as either; often we do both: show $ value and token-equivalent, e.g. 1M tokens or $15k, whichever runs out first. We also include a clause that any overage during pilot is billed at a reduced pilot rate unless we agree to top-up credits.
[03:20] Mark Rivera: What about termination or IP? We need assurances about data retention and that customer prompts aren't used to train public models.
[03:27] Jordan Lee: In Redwood Private and Dedicated modes, customer data is isolated; we have controls for data retention and don't use prompt data for model training without explicit opt-in. For hosted we can offer stricter retention policies for pilot datasets and options to sign an addendum — we'll include language in the security pack.
[03:45] Priya Sharma: Security is big — SOC 2, SSO (SAML), KMS for keys, audit logs — we need to sign off with our InfoSec.
[03:54] Samira Patel: Totally, we'll send our SOC 2 report and our security overview. Jordan will share the KMS options and the level of key access.
[04:05] Jordan Lee: One note: for VPC/private deployments there's an extra timeline for infra provisioning (usually 2-4 weeks) — if you require on-prem or VPC we should align procurement earlier.
[04:18] Liam O'Neill: How do you usually measure quality during a pilot? We have human evals but need an automated signal too.
[04:26] Jordan Lee: We'll run side-by-side evaluations against your baseline on a holdout set and produce both human and automatic metrics (ROUGE/BLEU-ish proxies and custom rubric). We can also do A/B routing for live traffic to compare.
[04:40] Mark Rivera: Latency target — we want P95 <250ms for shorter prompts and maybe <400ms for the 1k token cases. Is that achievable on hosted?
[04:50] Jordan Lee: On hosted with optimized kernels and batching we often hit ~150-300ms P95 for 512 token requests on modern GPU variants; long 1k token tails will be higher but we can use KV cache and prefix caching to reduce repeated context cost. Dedicated instances reduce variability and can tighten the P95.
[05:10] Priya Sharma: Cost target: currently around $0.0012 per token equivalent, we'd like to get under $0.0006 to be compelling. Any chance?
[05:20] Samira Patel: With quantized model variants, batching and proper routing, we've seen 30-60% cost reductions vs raw API usage — hitting $0.0006 is feasible depending on model selection and request mix. We'll recommend model/quantization profile in the benchmark plan.
[05:37] Rosa Kim: For legal, we need an SOW and a standard PO process. How does Redwood prefer to receive the PO?
[05:44] Samira Patel: We accept POs after initial commercial terms are approved; we send a short SOW + statement of work for the pilot, and procurement can route a PO to our finance team. If you need an MSA we have a standard MSA template but for pilots often the SOW plus security addenda suffices.
[06:02] Mark Rivera: Timeline constraints: procurement blackout mid-July — does that block the pilot start?
[06:09] Rosa Kim: Yes, if we don't have PO signed by July 10th our finance team won't process charges until after blackout.
[06:16] Samira Patel: We can still start some technical onboarding before the PO if Evergreen is comfortable — e.g., set up service accounts, send test prompts, run internal sims — but full benchmark runs that produce billable usage would be post-PO. Alternatively we can front-load free credits to run early tests.
[06:34] Priya Sharma: That would help. For benchmarking, what's the usual cadence and what metrics will you deliver?
[06:41] Jordan Lee: We'll run an initial single-node perf run for latency and then scale to concurrency to measure p50/p95/p99, throughput, tokens/sec and steady-state cost. We'll deliver a benchmark report with graphs and model configuration recommendations.
[06:56] Liam O'Neill: On the commercial guardrails, what if we need an extension? Will credits roll over?
[07:03] Samira Patel: Extensions are possible; often we add a short extension credit package or convert to a short-term paid pilot. We'll call it out in the SOW: optional 2-week extension for an agreed credit top-up.
[07:17] Mark Rivera: Who owns support during the pilot? We want an SE touch and on-call for initial runs.
[07:22] Jordan Lee: Jordan (me) will be primary SE support for the benchmark. We can also offer office hours and a dedicated Slack channel for the duration.
[07:33] Priya Sharma: Ok let's talk numbers quickly — you suggested $15k or 1M tokens. If we run more than 1M tokens during the pilot unintentionally, what's the rate?
[07:45] Samira Patel: The overage rate is typically a reduced pilot rate, e.g. 50% of standard hosted price for the duration of the pilot; we'll list exact numbers in the quote. We can also add a hard cap to prevent surprise usage.
[07:58] Rosa Kim: Hard cap is a must for procurement.
[08:02] Samira Patel: Noted — we'll include hard cap language and a notification threshold at 80% usage.
[08:11] Mark Rivera: For benchmarks can you support internal data residency needs? Some of our drivers' data is EU-located.
[08:19] Jordan Lee: We can run benchmarks in EU regions and pin the pilot to region-specific infra. For production we can offer Private or Dedicated with region isolation.
[08:31] Priya Sharma: One technical question: how do you handle KV cache consistency across nodes for long conversations?
[08:37] Jordan Lee: Our runtime has a distributed KV cache that keeps local hot keys with a coordinated invalidation for updates; for the pilot we'll instrument cache hit rates to show savings. There might be occasional cache misses during scale-up but it's measurable.
[08:55] Liam O'Neill: Any special integration work? We have an internal auth system.
[09:00] Samira Patel: We support SAML/SSO and API keys; for deeper integration we can do short lived tokens via your identity provider — Jordan will include an integration checklist.
[09:12] Rosa Kim: What's the path to procurement/contracting after pilot if we want to go Dedicated or Private?
[09:19] Samira Patel: After a successful pilot we typically propose an initial reserved capacity commitment or a license for Private, depending on needs. We'll produce a recommendation with pricing options: reserved monthly capacity (with commit discounts) vs. self-managed Private deployment. That will trigger the standard contracting process — MSA + SOW + ordering document.
[09:38] Mark Rivera: Does Redwood provide SLAs for Dedicated?
[09:42] Jordan Lee: Yes Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets, monitoring, and priority support. We'll include the SLA summary in the follow-up pack.
[09:52] Priya Sharma: One more on metrics: can you instrument cost by route/token-level so we can attribute cost to features?
[09:59] Jordan Lee: Yes Redwood Console has token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards; we can enable the relevant dashboards for the pilot and share read-only access.
[10:12] Samira Patel: Ok to summarize commercial guardrails we're proposing: 6-week pilot, $15k or 1M token credit, hard cap option, notification at 80%, optional 2-week extension credit, standard SOW + security pack, accepted PO to start billable runs, and SE support for benchmarks.
[10:34] Rosa Kim: That covers my questions. Will you send the SOW and the security docs?
[10:38] Samira Patel: Yes — Samira will share pilot quote + SOW + SOC2 + security overview. Jordan will share the benchmark plan and integration checklist.
[10:46] Mark Rivera: We'll aim to get prompts and traffic shape to you by June 30th. Procurement will try to slot PO before July 10th but will update.
[10:55] Samira Patel: Great. Any blockers from anyone?
[11:00] Priya Sharma: Just need the benchmark scripts and the ability to run an EU-region test; otherwise good.
[11:07] Jordan Lee: We'll provision EU test infra as part of the bench plan.
[11:12] Liam O'Neill: Sounds good.
[11:15] Samira Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the action items.

[11:30] --- end of recording note: the timestamps above are a rough alignment to the audio; some speaker labels may be imperfect due to transcription.
